rows.evidence: Q1: Methods/Results (Sections 2-3) - the authors build their own SWAT model of the Lower Mekong forced with TRMM/GPM precipitation and GLDAS temperature, calibrate it (2005-2006) and validate it (2001-2004, 2007-2015) against MRC gauge discharge at six sub-basin outlets. Q2: Section 3.2, Figs 3-5 - the satellite-forced model is compared with observed daily/monthly streamflow (NSE 0.86-0.95 in validation, ~3.85% monthly error; captured timing of onset and end of seasonal flow, slightly off on some peaks); Section 3.3, Table 5 and Fig. 10 - the model is used to compute high-flow disturbance metrics (7-day maximum flow, flood duration above MRC flood-stage thresholds, flood occurrence frequency) under upstream release scenarios. Q6: Section 2.1, Table 2 - the result is reported for the whole Lower Mekong basin (drainage area up to 656,518 km2 at Kratie) and six sub-basins across Thailand, Laos and Cambodia. Q7: Section 3.2 - the authors found that running the model without adjusting the remote-sensing precipitation overestimated streamflow by about 13%, so a separate precipitation correction factor per sub-basin was required (model most sensitive to these factors). Q8: Discussion (Section 4) - model results are uncertain owing to errors in input data, parameters and process representation; performance comparison was on monthly flows, so temporal/spatial aggregation may have masked individual event prediction.
rows.notes: Q2 is given with some doubt: the study validates satellite-forced streamflow simulations against gauges and derives flood-threshold exceedance and 7-day maximum metrics, but it does not directly score the skill of predicting the timing or magnitude of specific flood or drought events; the flood/drought 'predictability' results (Colwell index) concern flow-regime predictability under hypothetical upstream release scenarios rather than forecasting with remote sensing. Q3 no: single method (one model vs gauges). Q4 no: no separate intermediate variable isolated (e.g., no comparison of satellite vs gauge precipitation effect). Q5 no: six nested sub-basins along one river in one basin, not distinct climates/regions. Q9 no: only NSE/percent error reported for the model; standard deviations in Table 2 refer to observed annual discharge, not to the prediction result; SUFI2 used but no uncertainty bands reported.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2-3 - own SWAT model runs forced with satellite data and validated against observed discharge.
rows.notes: The study does not evaluate the use of remote sensing information for allocating water resources or any water-conservation outcome. It simulates Lower Mekong streamflow variability, predictability (Colwell index), flow reversals, 7-day maximum flow and flood duration under hypothetical +/-30% upstream inflow scenarios, and notes that the model could aid water accounting and guide decision makers. This provides hydrological information that is at most a precondition for allocation decisions; no allocation efficiency is tested or measured.

notes: Full text appears complete (abstract through references and appendices). The study is a basin-scale hydrological modeling paper using satellite precipitation/temperature as forcing; the 'extreme events' content is flood duration/frequency and flow predictability metrics, not an operational flood/drought forecast evaluation.
